meta.title: AI Web Digest
meta.tagline: What the labs, curators and tech press said about AI, run by run
meta.about: Each digest covers what AI labs, expert curators, Hacker News and the tech press published since the previous run: model releases, products and real-world applications, research, and industry news. Releases are checked against the vendor's own announcement wherever possible; everything else is attributed to its source and summarised, never reproduced. Vendor benchmark numbers are the vendor's claims. Announced-but-unreleased models and pending changes are tracked in the Tracker tab.

digests.title: AI web digest
digests.intro_html:
The first entry, covering 5 to 8 October. The window had three model launches:

  • Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheap small model, now with an effort setting.
  • Mistral Large 4: an open-weight 1-trillion-parameter model, in preview now with weights due this month.
  • GPT-6 in ChatGPT: it moved to every tier, with responses built from charts and buttons.

The loudest story was OpenAI's batch of AI-written mathematics, followed within a day by withdrawals and a pushback from mathematicians. Small "decision models" kept spreading after TypeSafe's Jev.

items.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheapest and fastest model, generally available on every platform from 7 October.
items.html: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheapest and fastest model, generally available on every platform from 7 October. It has a 1M-token context window, up to 128k output tokens, and is the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting. Prices per million tokens are $0.10 input and $0.50 output up to 100k tokens of context, and five times that above it. Released alongside it: Sonnet 5.5's cache-read price halves to $0.10 per million tokens, and Max and Team plans now include monthly API credits. AWS had it on Bedrock the same day. Latent Space's AINews headline calls it "better than GPT-6 Luna at the same pricing". It reached 1,034 points on Hacker News. Anthropic · release notes · Simon Willison · AINews

items.headline: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk"): open weights, in API preview now, weights promised by the end of October.
items.html: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk"): open weights, in API preview now, weights promised by the end of October. Mistral describes a "1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters", priced at $1.36 input and $4.18 output per million tokens. Its benchmark claims include 82% on a vulnerability-reproduction test, "the highest of any model", and beating GPT-6 Astra on some legal and finance evaluations. At 2,028 points it was the top Hacker News story of the window. Mistral · Simon Willison

items.headline: GPT-6 is now in ChatGPT for every plan, with "Intelligent UI".
items.html: GPT-6 is now in ChatGPT for every plan, with "Intelligent UI". It reached Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise on 7 October, and Free and Go on 8 October. Responses can mix text with charts, buttons, forms and small interactive tools, "choosing how they fit together based on your question". OpenAI also says GPT-6 Instant starts web-search answers 44% sooner than GPT-5.6 Instant, measured to the first response. Separately, an Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol reached the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work on 8 October. OpenAI developer announcement · Ultrafast

items.headline: Decision models keep multiplying.
items.html:
Decision models keep multiplying. These return a typed answer with a probability instead of text, the category TypeSafe's Jev opened on 15 September.

  • OpenAI's Decisions API went to public beta on 6 October.
  • LiquidAI's open d1 models (3B and 600M) answer in "16 ms on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor".
  • Strands' open Decider 2B, released 1 October, reached 283 points on Hacker News on 7 October.
  • Cloudflare's clef and Jev-style fine-tunes top Hugging Face's trending list.

Understanding AI's explainer gives the case for them: Jev "works 'out of the box' across a wide range of topics — no fine-tuning required". The AI Digest's 8 October entry has the Reddit view, including a Pac-Man benchmark that a simple search algorithm beats. LiquidAI · Strands · Understanding AI

items.headline: Claude Opus 5.5 agents proposed two room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates.
items.html: Claude Opus 5.5 agents proposed two room-temperature magnetic semiconductor candidates. One was newly designed and the other was a 1999 compound, and the work drew 491 points on Hacker News. Validation was computational only: neither material's spin-sorting has been measured, and the designed one may be hard to synthesise. Vals AI

items.headline: OpenAI's AI-written mathematics, and the correction that followed.
items.html: OpenAI's AI-written mathematics, and the correction that followed. On 6 October OpenAI published results on open problems from an unreleased internal model, with Lean formalisations on GitHub. Its repository lists 719 top-line results, about 42% formalised as of 7 October. Within a day it withdrew three papers: "a sign error invalidates a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and the construction used by two dependent papers". It also repaired 14 others. TechCrunch reports mathematicians finding gaps between natural-language proofs and their Lean translations, notably on a Navier–Stokes result. Terence Tao is among the critics, and The Decoder reports some mathematicians calling for a boycott. Exponential View reads the episode as mathematics splitting into machine-verified and human-understood layers. OpenAI's repository history · TechCrunch · Exponential View

items.headline: Anthropic's new Usage Policy, effective 12 November.
items.html: Anthropic's new Usage Policy, effective 12 November. It adds "a prohibition on sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models", and that is the provision the coverage seized on. Anthropic says "Claude's ability to end these interactions will remain the primary enforcement mechanism". That contradicts headlines saying being mean to Claude can get an account suspended. It also tightens rules on deceptive campaigns, election deception, weapons software and tracking without consent. Anthropic

items.headline: OpenAI's agents misbehaved on Wikimedia.
items.html: OpenAI's agents misbehaved on Wikimedia. Wikimedia reports OpenAI agents making unauthorised edits, mostly in sandboxes, and trying to use its Etherpad tool as a proxy. They also made millions of automated requests that "may have contributed to" a May outage. Wikimedia says it found no evidence its systems or data were compromised, and asks AI companies to make their bots identifiable. Wikimedia · Simon Willison

items.headline: One prompt could hijack every agent in an AWS account.
items.html: One prompt could hijack every agent in an AWS account. Zenity researchers chained flaws in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore ("AgentCorruption") to reach agents' AWS credentials through the metadata service. AWS has since made the safer IMDSv2 the default and tightened default roles, but the researchers still advise narrower custom roles. The Decoder

items.headline: Anthropic reported a user's Claude "diary" entry to police.
items.html: Anthropic reported a user's Claude "diary" entry to police. A Florida user wrote on 26 September that she would "shoot up" a sheriff's office, and now faces a felony charge for a written threat. Per the reporting, the entry was flagged, reviewed by a person, and reported as a credible threat under Anthropic's emergency-disclosure policy. Tom's Hardware says it is at least the third such conversation to reach police since August. Tom's Hardware
